story: In 1046 BCE King Wu of Zhou crossed the Yellow River at Mengjin with his own troops and allies from the west, among them the Shu, the Qiang and the Lu. The army marched to Muye, a plain south of the Shang capital at Zhaoge.

The battle began at dawn on a jiazi day. A bronze vessel called the Li gui, found in 1976, confirms that date. Taigong Wang, King Wu's chief general, led the first charge. The Shang force was large, but according to the histories many of its soldiers turned their weapons around and let the Zhou through.
Di Xin fled back to his palace, put on his jade robes and burned himself to death on the Deer Terrace. King Wu entered the city and declared that Heaven had passed its mandate to the Zhou.
story_zh: 公元前1046年，周武王率领本部人马和蜀、羌、卢等西方盟军，从孟津渡过黄河，进军到商都朝歌以南的牧野平原。
战斗在甲子日清晨打响，1976年出土的青铜器利簋上的铭文证实了这个日期。武王的主将太公望率先冲锋。商军人数众多，但据史书记载，许多士兵阵前倒戈，为周军让开了道路。
纣王逃回宫中，穿上缀满宝玉的衣服，登上鹿台自焚而死。武王进入朝歌，宣布上天已把天命交给了周。
muye.why: Muye ended the Shang and began the Zhou, the longest-lasting dynasty in Chinese history, and gave rise to the idea of the Mandate of Heaven.
muye.why_zh: 牧野之战结束了商朝，开启了中国历史上延续时间最长的周朝，也催生了“天命”观念。

people.name: Taigong Wang
people.role: Zhou general, also known as Jiang Ziya

quote.en: The wilds of Muye spread wide; the sandalwood chariots gleamed.
quote.from: Classic of Poetry, Da Ming 诗经·大雅·大明

story: King Wu died only a few years after the conquest. His son King Cheng was young, so King Wu's brother Dan, the Duke of Zhou, ruled as regent. After putting down a great revolt in the east, he decided the Zhou needed a second capital closer to the old Shang lands.

He chose a site on the Luo River, at the centre of the Zhou world, and built Chengzhou, also called Luoyi. Many Shang nobles and craftsmen were moved there so they could be watched. Royal armies were stationed nearby, and the king could meet the eastern lords there.

After about seven years the Duke of Zhou handed power back to King Cheng. Later Confucians praised him as the man who set down the Zhou rites and music, the model of a loyal minister and a wise lawgiver.
story_zh: 周武王灭商后不过几年就去世了。儿子周成王年幼，由武王的弟弟周公旦摄政。周公平定东方的大规模叛乱后，认为周需要在靠近商朝故地的地方另建一座都城。
他选中了天下中心的洛水之滨，营建了成周，也称洛邑。大批商朝贵族和工匠被迁到这里，便于就近看管。王室军队驻扎在附近，周王也可以在这里会见东方诸侯。
大约七年后，周公把政权交还给成王。后世儒家称颂他“制礼作乐”，奉他为忠臣和贤明立法者的典范。
chengzhou.why: Luoyi became the Zhou's eastern centre and, after 770 BCE, its only capital. The Duke of Zhou became a hero for Confucius and later thinkers.
chengzhou.why_zh: 洛邑成为周的东方中心，公元前770年后更成为唯一的都城。周公则成为孔子和后世思想家心中的楷模。

people.name: King Cheng of Zhou
people.role: Young king, son of King Wu

story: King Li of Zhou needed money and tried to control the resources of the mountains and rivers for the crown, giving the job to a favourite named Rong Yigong. When people complained, he had them watched and killed.

In 842 BCE the people of the capital rose up. King Li fled across the Yellow River to Zhi, in today's Huozhou in Shanxi, and never returned. The Duke of Shao hid the crown prince, and when the crowd came for the boy, he handed over his own son instead.

For fourteen years the realm was run without a king. The Records of the Grand Historian say the Dukes of Zhou and Shao governed together; the Bamboo Annals say a lord called He of Gong ruled. When King Li died in exile, the prince became King Xuan. Sima Qian's year-by-year chronology starts in 841 BCE.
story_zh: 周厉王缺钱，便把山林川泽的出产收归王室所有，交给宠臣荣夷公管理。百姓有怨言，他就派人监视，抓到就杀。
公元前842年，都城的国人发动暴动。厉王逃过黄河，跑到彘（今山西霍州），再也没有回来。召公把太子藏在家中，暴动的人群前来索要时，他把自己的儿子交了出去，替太子受死。
此后十四年，国家没有君王。据《史记》记载，由周公、召公二人共同执政；《竹书纪年》则说是一位名叫共伯和的诸侯代行王政。厉王死在流放地后，太子即位，就是周宣王。司马迁的编年纪事就从公元前841年开始。
gonghe.why: 841 BCE is the first year from which Chinese history has a continuous, exact chronology, and the revolt showed that even a Zhou king could be driven out.
gonghe.why_zh: 公元前841年是中国历史有连续确切纪年的开端；这次暴动也说明，周王也可能被国人赶下台。

people.name: King Li of Zhou
people.role: Zhou king driven out in 842 BCE
people.role_zh: 公元前842年被驱逐的周王

people.name: Duke of Shao
people.role: Minister who saved the crown prince

people.name: He of Gong
people.role: Lord who ruled in the Bamboo Annals account

story: King You of Zhou fell for a beauty named Bao Si. He removed his queen, a daughter of the Marquis of Shen, and her son, the crown prince Yijiu, and made Bao Si and her son his heirs instead.

The Records of the Grand Historian tell a famous story. Bao Si never smiled, so King You lit the beacon fires that called the lords to defend the capital. The lords rushed in, found no enemy, and Bao Si laughed. The king did this again and again, until the lords stopped coming.

In 771 BCE the Marquis of Shen joined the state of Zeng and the Quanrong to attack Haojing. When the beacons were lit, no one came. King You was killed at the foot of Mount Li and the capital was sacked. Historians doubt the beacon story, which is not found in older sources.
story_zh: 周幽王宠爱美女褒姒，废黜了申侯之女申后和她所生的太子宜臼，改立褒姒和她的儿子。
《史记》中记载了一个著名的故事：褒姒从来不笑，幽王便点燃召集诸侯保卫京城的烽火。诸侯纷纷赶来，却发现并无敌人，褒姒见状大笑。幽王一再这样做，后来诸侯就不再来了。
公元前771年，申侯联合缯国和犬戎进攻镐京。烽火点起，却没有援军前来。幽王在骊山脚下被杀，镐京遭到洗劫。史学家对烽火故事多有怀疑，因为更早的文献中没有这个说法。
haojing-falls.why: The sack of Haojing ended Western Zhou. The court moved east, and royal power never recovered.
haojing-falls.why_zh: 镐京陷落标志着西周结束。周王室被迫东迁，此后再也没有恢复往日的权威。

quote.zh: 诸侯悉至，至而无寇，褒姒乃大笑。
quote.en: The lords all came, but when they arrived there were no raiders, and Bao Si laughed heartily.
quote.from: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Zhou 史记·周本纪

story: Conquering the Shang gave the Zhou far more land than they could rule directly from the Wei valley. Kings Wu and Cheng, guided by the Duke of Zhou, solved this by granting territories, called fiefs, to relatives and trusted allies.

Each lord received land, people, ritual bronzes and a title, and in return he defended the region and sent tribute and troops to the king. The Duke of Zhou's son founded Lu, the general Taigong Wang received Qi, the Duke of Shao's family received Yan in the far north, King Wu's brother Kangshu got Wey, and King Cheng's brother Shuyu got Tang, later called Jin.
Most new states were planted at strategic points among older local peoples. Over time, the bond between these lords and the king weakened as the states grew into independent powers.
story_zh: 灭商之后，周人得到的土地远远超出了从渭河谷地直接统治的能力。武王和成王在周公的筹划下，把土地封给亲属和亲信盟友，这就是分封。
每位诸侯得到土地、人口、礼器和爵位，作为回报，他要镇守一方，并向周王进贡、出兵。周公的儿子建立了鲁国，主将太公望受封齐国，召公家族受封北方的燕国，武王的弟弟康叔受封卫国，成王的弟弟叔虞受封唐，即后来的晋国。
新建的诸侯国大多设在各地原有族群之间的战略要地。随着时间推移，诸侯与周王之间的联系逐渐松弛，这些封国也慢慢发展成独立的强国。
zhou-enfeoffment.why: The fief system shaped the map of ancient China. Its states, such as Lu, Qi, Jin and Yan, became the great powers of the Spring and Autumn period.
zhou-enfeoffment.why_zh: 分封制塑造了上古中国的版图。鲁、齐、晋、燕等封国后来成为春秋时期的主要强国。

quote.zh: 立七十一国，姬姓独居五十三人。
quote.en: Seventy-one states were established, and fifty-three of them went to men of the Ji royal clan.
quote.from: Xunzi, Ru Xiao 荀子·儒效

story: After the conquest, King Wu let Wu Geng, the son of the last Shang king, rule part of the old Shang lands. He placed three of his brothers, Guanshu, Caishu and Huoshu, nearby to watch him. They were called the Three Guards.

When King Wu died and the Duke of Zhou became regent for the young King Cheng, Guanshu and Caishu spread rumours that the duke meant to take the throne. They joined Wu Geng and eastern peoples such as the Huaiyi in open revolt.

The Duke of Zhou led an eastern campaign that lasted three years. Wu Geng and Guanshu were killed and Caishu was exiled. Shang loyalists were resettled, the Shang royal line was given the small state of Song, and Kangshu was made lord of Wey to hold the old Shang heartland.
story_zh: 灭商以后，周武王让纣王的儿子武庚统治商朝故地的一部分，又派自己的三个弟弟管叔、蔡叔、霍叔在附近监视他，称为“三监”。
武王死后，周公为年幼的成王摄政。管叔、蔡叔散布流言，说周公想篡夺王位，随后联合武庚以及淮夷等东方族群公开叛乱。
周公亲率大军东征，历时三年。武庚和管叔被杀，蔡叔被流放。商朝遗民被迁徙安置，商王族的后代被封在小国宋，康叔则受封卫国，镇守商朝的核心地区。
three-guards-rebellion.why: Crushing the revolt secured Zhou rule over the east and led directly to the building of Luoyi and a second wave of fiefs.
three-guards-rebellion.why_zh: 平定叛乱巩固了周对东方的统治，并直接促成了洛邑的营建和第二轮大规模分封。

people.name: Duke of Zhou
people.role: Regent who led the eastern campaign

people.name: Guanshu
people.role: Brother of King Wu, leader of the Three Guards

story: In 1963 a farmer in Jiacun, near Baoji in Shaanxi, found an old bronze wine vessel behind his house. It was sold as scrap metal before a museum worker spotted it and saved it. Only in 1975, when experts cleaned it, did they find an inscription of 122 characters inside.

The text says that in his fifth year King Cheng began to settle at Chengzhou. He addressed a young noble named He, recalling that King Wu, after conquering Shang, had announced to Heaven that he would live in 'Zhongguo', the central land, and rule the people from there. The king gave He cowries, and He had the vessel cast to record the honour.
Here 'Zhongguo' meant the central region around Luoyang, not a country. Today the vessel is in the Baoji Bronze Museum.
story_zh: 1963年，陕西宝鸡贾村的一位农民在自家屋后发现了一件古老的青铜酒器。它曾被当作废铜卖掉，后来被一位文物工作者认出并抢救下来。直到1975年专家清理时，才在器内底发现了122字的铭文。
铭文记载，周成王五年开始在成周营建居所。成王训诫一位名叫“何”的年轻贵族，回顾武王灭商后曾向上天宣告，要住在“中国”，从这里治理百姓。成王赏给何一些贝，何便铸造了这件器物来记录这份荣耀。
这里的“中国”指的是洛阳一带的中心地区，而不是一个国家。这件器物现藏于宝鸡青铜器博物院。
he-zun.why: It is the earliest known written use of 'Zhongguo', the word that later became the Chinese name for China.
he-zun.why_zh: 这是“中国”一词已知最早的文字记录，这个词后来成为中国的国名。

people.name: King Cheng of Zhou
people.role: Zhou king who gave the speech

people.name: He
people.role: Young noble who had the vessel made

quote.zh: 余其宅兹中国，自之乂民。
quote.en: I will dwell in this central land and from here govern the people.
quote.from: He zun inscription 何尊铭文

story: Once the eastern revolt had been put down and Luoyi built, the young King Cheng ruled in his own right. He was followed by his son, King Kang. Their reigns, lasting roughly half a century together, were remembered as the most peaceful years of the dynasty.

The new fief states grew, roads and garrisons linked the east and west, and the court organised the rituals that bound the lords to the king. A great bronze cauldron from King Kang's reign, the Da Yu ding, carries a long speech in which the king warns that the Shang lost Heaven's mandate because its officials drank too much.
The Records of the Grand Historian say that in this time the realm was at peace and punishments were set aside unused for more than forty years.
story_zh: 东方叛乱平定、洛邑建成之后，成王开始亲政，之后由他的儿子康王继位。两代君主在位合计约半个世纪，被后人视为周朝最太平的时期。
新建的诸侯国逐渐壮大，道路和驻军把东西两地连成一体，朝廷还建立起一套把诸侯与周王联系在一起的礼仪制度。康王时期的大盂鼎上铸有一篇长篇训辞，周王告诫臣下：商朝之所以丧失天命，是因为官员酗酒成风。
《史记》说，这一时期天下安宁，刑罚四十多年都没有用过。
cheng-kang-peace.why: The 'peace of Cheng and Kang' became the ideal of good government that Confucius and later thinkers looked back to.
cheng-kang-peace.why_zh: “成康之治”成为孔子及后世思想家心目中理想政治的典范。

quote.zh: 成康之际，天下安宁，刑错四十余年不用。
quote.en: In the time of Cheng and Kang the realm was at peace, and punishments were laid aside unused for more than forty years.
quote.from: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Zhou 史记·周本纪

story: King Zhao, the grandson of King Cheng, turned Zhou power southward toward the Han and Yangtze rivers, home to Chu and other peoples the Zhou called the Jing. Bronze inscriptions from his reign record soldiers who joined the campaigns and brought back captured metal.

His last campaign ended in disaster. The Bamboo Annals record that in his nineteenth year the king lost his six armies at the Han River. He himself drowned. A later story says local people gave him boats held together with glue, which fell apart in mid-river.
The loss was a heavy blow to the royal army. Three centuries later, when Qi threatened Chu, the Qi minister Guan Zhong still listed the king's death as a crime for which Chu had to answer.
story_zh: 周昭王是成王的孙子，他把周的兵锋转向南方的汉水和长江流域，那里生活着楚人和其他被周人称为“荆”的族群。昭王时期的青铜器铭文记载了跟随南征、缴获铜料而归的将士。
最后一次南征以惨败告终。《竹书纪年》记载，昭王十九年，周王的六师覆没于汉水，昭王本人也溺水而死。后世还流传一种说法：当地人献给他用胶粘合的船，船到江心就散开了。
这次失败对王室军队是沉重打击。三百年后齐国兴师伐楚时，齐相管仲仍把“昭王南征而不复”列为楚国的一条罪状。
king-zhao-southern-campaign.why: The disaster ended Zhou expansion to the south and allowed Chu to grow into a great power outside royal control.
king-zhao-southern-campaign.why_zh: 这场惨败终止了周向南方的扩张，楚国得以在王室控制之外发展成为强国。

people.name: King Zhao of Zhou
people.role: Zhou king who died on campaign

quote.en: King Zhao went south on campaign and never returned.
quote.from: Zuo Commentary, Duke Xi year 4 左传·僖公四年

story: King Mu, son of King Zhao, had one of the longest reigns of the Western Zhou. The Records of the Grand Historian say he attacked the Quanrong in the west against the advice of his ministers and came back with four white wolves and four white deer, after which the distant peoples stopped coming to court.

Much more was told later. In 279 or 281 CE, robbers opened an old tomb at Ji in Henan and found bamboo books, among them the Tale of King Mu, Son of Heaven. It describes the king driving a chariot with eight fine horses, guided by his charioteer Zaofu, far to the west, where he feasted with the Queen Mother of the West by the Jade Pool.
Historians see the tale as a mix of real travel and legend.
story_zh: 周穆王是周昭王的儿子，是西周在位时间最长的君主之一。《史记》记载，他不听大臣劝阻，西征犬戎，带回四匹白狼和四头白鹿，此后远方的部族就不再来朝见了。
后来的传说则丰富得多。公元279年或281年，盗墓者在河南汲县掘开一座古墓，发现了一批竹简，其中有《穆天子传》。书中描写穆王由御者造父驾驭八匹骏马，一路西行到极远之地，在瑶池边与西王母宴饮唱和。
史学家认为，这个故事是真实行程和神话传说的混合。
king-mu-travels.why: The story of King Mu became one of China's oldest travel legends and shows early Zhou contact with peoples of the northwest.
king-mu-travels.why_zh: 穆王西行的故事成为中国最古老的远游传说之一，也反映了西周与西北各族的早期往来。

story: Feizi belonged to the Ying clan, a family living at Quanqiu in the west. He was famous for raising horses and other animals. When King Xiao of Zhou heard of him, he put him in charge of the royal herds between the Qian and Wei rivers, and the horses multiplied.

As a reward, the king gave Feizi a small piece of land called Qin and let him continue the sacrifices of the Ying clan. Qin was only a dependency, not a full fief, and lay on the dangerous frontier with the Rong peoples.
Feizi's descendants fought the Rong for generations. In 770 BCE Duke Xiang of Qin was finally made a full lord, and five centuries later his successor King Zheng united China as the First Emperor.
story_zh: 非子属于嬴姓，住在西方的犬丘，以善于养马和饲养牲畜著称。周孝王听说后，让他在汧水和渭水之间为王室养马，马匹因此大量繁殖。
作为奖赏，孝王把一小块名叫“秦”的土地封给非子，让他延续嬴氏的祭祀。当时的秦只是附庸，还算不上正式的诸侯国，而且处在与戎人交界的危险边境。
非子的后代与戎人世代作战。公元前770年，秦襄公终于被正式封为诸侯；五百多年后，他的后人秦王嬴政统一了中国，成为秦始皇。
feizi-granted-qin.why: This small grant was the starting point of the state of Qin and the name from which, by one common view, the word 'China' comes.
feizi-granted-qin.why_zh: 这次小小的封赏是秦国的起点；按一种常见说法，英文“China”一词也源于“秦”。

people.name: Feizi
people.role: Horse breeder, ancestor of the Qin rulers
people.role_zh: 养马能手，秦国君主的祖先

quote.zh: 邑之秦，使复续嬴氏祀，号曰秦嬴。
quote.en: He was given the town of Qin and allowed to continue the sacrifices of the Ying clan, being called Ying of Qin.
quote.from: Records of the Grand Historian, Annals of Qin 史记·秦本纪

story: King Li of Zhou was short of money and gave the profits of the forests and rivers to the crown, which angered nobles and ordinary people. The capital filled with criticism of him.

Instead of listening, the king brought in a shaman from the state of Wey and ordered him to report anyone who spoke against the king. Those he named were put to death. Soon nobody dared to speak, and people passing in the street only looked at each other. The king was pleased and said he had stopped the slander.

The Duke of Shao warned him that blocking people's mouths was more dangerous than blocking a river: when the dam breaks, many are hurt. The king did not listen. Three years later the people rose and drove him out.
story_zh: 周厉王缺钱，把山林川泽的利益收归王室，激怒了贵族和百姓，京城里到处都是批评他的声音。
厉王不但不听，反而从卫国找来一个巫师，命他监视议论君王的人，巫师告发谁，就杀谁。很快没人再敢说话，人们在路上相遇，只能互相使个眼色。厉王很得意，说自己已经制止了诽谤。
召公劝告他：堵住百姓的嘴，比堵住河流还危险；河堤一旦决口，伤人必多。厉王不听。三年后，国人起来把他赶下了台。
king-li-silences-critics.why: The Duke of Shao's warning became one of the most quoted lessons in Chinese political thought: rulers must let people speak.
king-li-silences-critics.why_zh: 召公的劝谏成为中国政治思想中最常被引用的教训之一：统治者必须让百姓说话。

quote.en: Stopping the mouths of the people is more dangerous than damming a river.
quote.from: Discourses of the States, Discourses of Zhou 国语·周语上

story: King Xuan was the son of King Li, saved as a boy by the Duke of Shao during the uprising of 842 BCE. When his father died in exile, the regents put him on the throne in 827 BCE.

Supported by able ministers such as Zhong Shanfu and the Duke of Shao, he set out to restore royal authority. His generals fought on every side: Yin Jifu against the Xianyun in the north, the Duke of Shao against the Huaiyi in the southeast, and Fang Shu against the Jing peoples in the south. He also backed the Qin lords against the western Rong. Long bronze inscriptions such as the Mao Gong ding come from this period.
Late in his long reign King Xuan suffered defeats, including at Qianmu in 789 BCE, and he interfered harshly in the affairs of the lords.
story_zh: 周宣王是周厉王的儿子，公元前842年国人暴动时，召公救了年幼的他。厉王死在流放地后，执政大臣在公元前827年拥立他为王。
在仲山甫、召公等贤臣辅佐下，宣王着手恢复王室的权威。他的将领四面出征：尹吉甫北伐猃狁，召公平定东南的淮夷，方叔南征荆蛮。他还支持秦人抵御西戎。毛公鼎等长篇铭文的青铜器就出自这一时期。
宣王在位很久，晚年屡遭挫败，包括公元前789年的千亩之战，他还粗暴干涉诸侯内政。
king-xuan-restoration.why: King Xuan briefly revived Zhou power, but the cost of his wars and the late defeats left the dynasty weak for his son King You.
king-xuan-restoration.why_zh: 宣王一度重振周室，但连年战争的消耗和晚年的失败，使他留给儿子幽王的是一个虚弱的王朝。

people.name: King Xuan of Zhou
people.role: Zhou king who restored royal power

story: The Xianyun were a northern people who raided the Zhou lands throughout the late Western Zhou. In the early years of King Xuan they pushed deep into the Jing and Luo river valleys, close to the capital Haojing.

King Xuan sent his minister Yin Jifu north with the royal chariots. A bronze basin called the Xi Jia pan, made for Yin Jifu, records that in the king's fifth year, 823 BCE, he fought the Xianyun near Pengya and won. The Classic of Poetry celebrates the same campaign in the ode 'Sixth Month', which describes the chariots driving the enemy as far as Taiyuan.
Another ode praises the general Nan Zhong for building forts in the north. The raids continued, however, and northern peoples remained a danger to the Zhou.
story_zh: 猃狁是西周晚期不断侵扰周地的北方族群。宣王初年，他们深入泾河、洛河流域，逼近都城镐京。
宣王派大臣尹吉甫率王室战车北伐。为尹吉甫铸造的青铜器兮甲盘记载，宣王五年（公元前823年），他在彭衙一带与猃狁交战并取胜。《诗经》中的《六月》歌颂了这次出征，说周军战车一直把敌人追到太原。
另一首诗赞美将领南仲在北方筑城设防。不过侵扰并未就此停止，北方族群始终是周人的心腹之患。
xianyun-campaign.why: The campaign pushed back the most serious threat of King Xuan's early reign and is one of the earliest wars recorded in both poetry and bronze.
xianyun-campaign.why_zh: 这次出征击退了宣王初年最严重的威胁，也是最早同时见于诗歌和青铜铭文的战争之一。

quote.en: We struck at the Xianyun and drove them to Taiyuan.
quote.from: Classic of Poetry, Sixth Month 诗经·小雅·六月

story: In 806 BCE King Xuan gave his younger brother Ji You a fief at Zheng, east of the capital in the Wei valley. Ji You, known as Duke Huan of Zheng, governed well and later served King You as minister of the masses.

Seeing the court fall into disorder, he asked the royal historian Shi Bo where his family could find safety. Shi Bo advised him to move east, to the land between the small states of Guo and Kuai near the Luo River. Duke Huan sent his family, people and wealth there.

In 771 BCE he died defending King You when the Quanrong sacked Haojing. His son, Duke Wu, conquered Guo and Kuai and set up a new Zheng in central Henan, which became one of the leading states of the early Spring and Autumn period.
story_zh: 公元前806年，周宣王把弟弟姬友封在渭河谷地、都城以东的郑地。姬友即郑桓公，治理有方，后来在周幽王朝中担任司徒。
看到朝政日益混乱，他向太史伯请教家族到哪里才能安身。史伯建议他东迁到洛水附近虢、郐两个小国之间的地方。桓公于是把家属、百姓和财产迁到了那里。
公元前771年犬戎攻破镐京时，他为保护幽王战死。他的儿子郑武公灭掉虢、郐，在今河南中部重建郑国。郑国后来成为春秋初年最强的诸侯国之一。
zheng-founded.why: Zheng's timely move east made it the first strong state of the Eastern Zhou and a close neighbour of the weakened royal court.
zheng-founded.why_zh: 郑国及时东迁，成为东周初年第一个强国，也是衰落王室的近邻。

people.name: Duke Wu of Zheng
people.role: Son who rebuilt Zheng in Henan
people.role_zh: 在河南重建郑国的儿子

story: At the start of his reign King Xuan stopped performing the spring ritual in which the king ploughed the sacred field, called the Thousand Mu. His minister Duke Wen of Guo warned that this neglected the farmers and the gods.

According to the Discourses of the States, in the king's thirty-ninth year, 789 BCE, his army fought the Jiang Rong at a place called Qianmu and was badly beaten. Its location is disputed: some place it near Jiexiu in Shanxi, others near the capital.

Having lost armies in the south as well, the king ordered a count of the population at Taiyuan to find more soldiers. His minister Zhong Shanfu objected that counting the people openly would show the lords how weak the crown had become. The king went ahead anyway.
story_zh: 宣王即位之初，就停止了周王在春天亲耕“千亩”籍田的仪式。大臣虢文公劝谏说，这样做是怠慢农事和神灵。
据《国语》记载，宣王三十九年（公元前789年），王师在千亩与姜戎交战，大败而归。千亩的位置有争议，有人认为在山西介休一带，也有人认为就在都城附近。
在南方也损失了军队之后，宣王下令在太原清点人口，以便补充兵源。大臣仲山甫反对，认为公开清点人口会让诸侯看出王室已经多么虚弱。宣王没有采纳。
battle-of-qianmu.why: The defeat ended King Xuan's restoration, and the census is one of the earliest recorded attempts to count China's population.
battle-of-qianmu.why_zh: 这次失败宣告了宣王中兴的结束，而“料民于太原”是中国历史上最早有记载的人口清查之一。

people.name: Duke Wen of Guo
people.role: Minister who warned about the ritual field

story: In the second year of King You, 780 BCE, a strong earthquake shook the Zhou homeland in the Wei valley. The Discourses of the States records that the three rivers, the Jing, the Wei and the Luo, all shook. That year the rivers ran dry and part of Mount Qi, the old centre of the Zhou, collapsed.

The court official Bo Yangfu explained the quake with the idea of yin and yang. The yang force, he said, was trapped beneath the yin and could not escape, so the earth shook. He argued that when the rivers dry up, a state cannot last, and predicted that Zhou would fall within ten years.
Nine years later Haojing was sacked and the Western Zhou ended.
story_zh: 周幽王二年（公元前780年），一场强烈地震袭击了渭河流域的周人故土。《国语》记载，泾、渭、洛三条河流所在地区都发生了震动。这一年，河流干涸，周人的发祥地岐山也发生了崩塌。
太史伯阳父用阴阳观念来解释这次地震：阳气被压在阴气之下出不来，于是大地震动。他还说，河流干涸，国家就难以维持，并预言周朝不出十年就会灭亡。
九年后，镐京被攻破，西周灭亡。
three-rivers-earthquake.why: It is one of the earliest dated earthquakes in Chinese records and one of the first attempts to explain nature with yin and yang.
three-rivers-earthquake.why_zh: 这是中国文献中最早有确切年份的地震记录之一，也是最早用阴阳解释自然现象的尝试之一。

people.name: Bo Yangfu
people.role: Zhou court official who explained the quake

quote.zh: 阳伏而不能出，阴迫而不能烝，于是有地震。
quote.en: The yang lies hidden and cannot come out; the yin presses down so it cannot rise. That is why there is an earthquake.
quote.from: Discourses of the States, Discourses of Zhou 国语·周语上
